quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: If you are in a crash, you must:

options.text: Stop at the crash scene or as close as possible without blocking traffic.
Report the crash to police as soon as possible.
Tell your insurance company right away.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In a crash, you must stop at the scene or as close as you can without blocking traffic. Help anyone who is hurt. Report the crash to police immediately. Exchange information with other people involved. Tell your insurance company right away.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use your parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a low ground railroad crossing. The railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is nearby.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down as you approach the intersection and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing yellow light. You should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop because the light is about to turn red.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and with caution. Look both ways for traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must let drivers who arrived before you go first.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, you must let drivers who got there before you enter the intersection first. Wait your turn.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children off, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you before you go.
Watch for children walking along the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: You reach an intersection that is blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Drive slowly through until traffic moves.
Get as close as you can to the car in front.
Do not enter the intersection until you can get all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can get all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side. Wait until the way is clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: You should increase your distance from the car in front when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
Leaving an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Increase your distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when leaving an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You are on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move over to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move over to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ends.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep grade ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill section is coming up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children who are too small for regular seat belts need special child seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always secure a child properly in a seat before driving.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if no sign forbids it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show a sharp curve in the direction of the arrow. In this case, the road curves sharply to the left. You may see several of these signs through a curve.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry, what should you do?

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't react with hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When drivers are angry, stay away from them physically and mentally. Avoid eye contact and don't make gestures that might provoke them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Decrease your speed.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, you must pull off and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: Motorcycles are small and hard to see. When pulling out into traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Never drive in a motorcyclist's lane.
Check twice for motorcycles.
Use extra caution before pulling out in front of a motorcycle.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Check twice for motorcycles before pulling into traffic. Always be extra careful when pulling out in front of a motorcycle.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your low beams.
Use your high beams.
It makes no difference which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes wrong.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, hurts your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, makes it harder to recover from headlight glare, and often makes you take more risks.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine work better on a cold.
The combination can greatly increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can greatly increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can increase how much both substances impair you. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine can affect you as much as several drinks would alone.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. You should be ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: T intersection ahead.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to road hazards. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming. Be ready to turn left or right.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking on the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that pedestrians cross at this location. Drive carefully where pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other vehicles.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic, signal and match the speed of other vehicles. Always yield to traffic already on the road.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through the middle on a regulatory sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drivers should go below the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. A red circle with a slash means that action is forbidden.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when should you proceed?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one of the tracks is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with more than one track, do not go as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: You are entering a crowded freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Check your side mirror, rearview mirror, and blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match freeway traffic.
Let freeway traffic go first.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Speed up on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic. Let traffic on the freeway go first. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have space to merge safely.

questions.question: What colors are warning signs that show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic go first, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What can make a person's driving ability worse?

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Not getting enough sleep.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Driving can be made worse by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and tiredness.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and dangers. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.
